merged.title: feat(ports): carry 100 functions over from Lombyte by machine (22.14%)
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

100 functions that Lombyte has matched in the US build, and whose PAL code is the same
instructions at other addresses, carried over without a model: 87 level functions and
13 functions of the executable, 68,796 bytes.

| | Before (upstream) | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Code matched | 20.24% (751,292 bytes) | 22.14% (821,928 bytes) |
| Functions | 2,834 / 5,109 | 2,936 / 5,109 |
| Fuzzy | 22.88% | 24.73% |
| Executable | 58.21% | 59.80% |
| Common level code | 22.16% | 26.07% |
| Level-specific code | 10.46% | 11.26% |

The other two functions in the count are `func_L16_002E45F8` (1,364 bytes, from the
Level 16 work) and your own `func_L07_00320CD0`, which the committed report had not
counted yet.

## How the ports were made

A tool (`tools/port.py` in OpenRAC) compares the US and PAL builds function by function.
Where the two are the same instructions, it takes Lombyte's C and:

- **renames every symbol** to its PAL name. It does not use a symbol tab

merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

140 more functions matched, 1,078,252 bytes of level code. The report goes from 2,974 to 3,114 of 5,109 functions and from 22.59% to 51.63% of the code. Upstream `main` (3848fd6) is merged in.

Most of the bytes are three functions that every level carries its own version of. Once one version was matched, the others were built from its C case by case.

**Long functions (57, by Opus long-function workers, `docs/LONG_FUNCTIONS.md`)**

- The hero's per-state movement function, `func_L00_002180F8` (39,324 bytes) and its 13 level versions. It is now matched everywhere it exists.
- The hero's state-setting function, `func_L02_0022BE40` (13,240 bytes), its 12 other level versions and the shared one. Also complete.
- The hero's update function, `func_L03_0021CDA8` (20,272 bytes) and 11 relatives, including `func_L00_0022A340` (33,312 bytes). Levels 05 and 16 are staged near misses, see below.
- 17 others between 0.9 and 12.8 KB, six of them finished b

merged.title: feat(include): qcopy_nc() and qzero(), and the 17 functions they unlock (51.63% to 53.10%)
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Two small helpers beside `qcopy()` in `include/common.h`, and the 17 functions that match with them: 54,460 bytes. The report goes from 3,114 to 3,131 of 5,109 functions and from 51.63% to 53.10% of the code.

## The helpers

- `qcopy_nc(dst, src)` is `qcopy()` without the `"memory"` clobber. Retail has both behaviours: the hero's state-setting function reloads a value after a copy, and the hero's update function keeps it in its register across one.
- `qzero(p)` is `sq $0,0(p)`, a 128-bit zero store. C always materialises the zero with `por` first. Lombyte identified it (its `include/qzero.h`), and the helper is credited there.

`qcopy()` itself is unchanged. Dropping its clobber was tried first: the executable stays identical, but eleven matched state-setting functions come out 8 bytes short.

## What matches with them

- `func_L16_00227818` (26,480 bytes) and `func_L05_00256148` (22,460 bytes), each with `qcopy_nc()` at one copy. They were 83 bytes off. The h

merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Level 17 (Drek's Fleet) is the first level whose own code is fully matched. Getting a level
unit to "complete" needed two changes to how the report treats level code, so those are in
here too, each as its own commit.

| | Before (#31) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Functions finished | 3,131 / 5,109 | 3,186 / 5,109 |
| Code matched | 53.10% | 54.43% |
| Fully linked | 4.66% | 8.45% |
| Units complete | 69 / 278 | 71 / 278 |

The 55 newly finished entries are 29 matched functions (49,404 bytes), 22 linker remnants
(88 bytes) and 4 pieces of joined functions (88 bytes).

## Needs a decision: two report rules

`docs/ASM_CLASSIFICATION.md` says a change to the published progress policy needs upstream
review. Both commits stand alone and can be dropped without touching the matches.

**`b130ecc` Level code's linker remnants count as finished, as the executable's do.**
Level code has the same leftovers the executable has: the one word the linker left of a
functio

merged.title: Merge platypet2217-star/RAC2Decomp and add NTSC/PAL region support
merged.author: Lynder063
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Merges the PAL functional decompilation from [platypet2217-star/RAC2Decomp](https://github.com/platypet2217-star/RAC2Decomp) into this repository and makes the tools region-aware (USA NTSC-U and Europe PAL).

1. **`merge:`** imports the full history of platypet2217-star/RAC2Decomp (`main` at `3e804dc`, 28 commits, original authorship kept) into `ports/pal-functional/` with a subtree merge. It is a non-matching reconstruction of `SCES_516.07`, so it stays outside `src/`, `candidates/`, catalogues and proofs, and adds no progress. Its MIT LICENSE (© platypet2217-star) is kept.
2. **`tools:`** adds `config/regions.json` and `scripts/region.py`. `setup.py`, `doctor.py`, `build.py`, `campaign_build.py`, `campaign.py` and `ApplyMobyNames.java` now resolve identities per region (`--region`, `RAC2_REGION`, or the manifest/catalogue serial). USA v1.01 stays the default and the only *matching* region; its identity files are byte-identical. PAL is registered but **unmeasured**. `setup

merged.title: ci: validate the exported progress report with objdiff
merged.author: Lynder063
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Both workflows upload `SCUS_972.68_report`, which decomp.dev parses with objdiff, but nothing checks that objdiff can load it. This adds one step after the export. It downloads `objdiff-cli` v3.8.1, pinned by SHA-256 (the same release and check as rac1-decomp's progress workflow), and runs `objdiff-cli report changes report.json report.json`. If the report does not load, the job fails before the upload.

It reads only the generated report: no game data, toolchain or hashed proof input changes.

## Validation

- Locally, objdiff-cli v3.8.1 (checksum verified) loads the report exported from current `RAC2` (`eeaf43b`) and exits 0.
- It exits 1 for three corrupted copies: a non-numeric `matchedCode`, a unit whose `measures` is a list, and a truncated file.
- Both workflow files parse as YAML.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

merged.title: research: record RAC1 fp-bit evidence for the boot runtime helpers
merged.author: Lynder063
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

`FUN_00123400` (144 B) and `FUN_001234F0` (64 B) are stopped with the reopening condition "independent original source/compiler evidence". Next to the integrated `FUN_00123268` (44 B), they have the sizes and order of fp-bit's `__make_dp`, `__unpack_f` and `fptodp` in RAC1.

[rac1-decomp](https://github.com/OpenRAC/rac1-decomp) matches all three on `SCES_509.16`, byte for byte. It compiles GCC 2.95.3's `fp-bit.c` **whole** with Sony's gcc 2.9-ee-991111 through its driver. The file is unmodified apart from two marked changes. The build uses fp-bit's own configuration macros (`-DFLOAT -DFLOAT_BIT_ORDER_MISMATCH -DNO_DENORMALS -DUS_SOFTWARE_GOFAST`), as Sony's `libgcc.a` build does.

This PR:
- adds `docs/RAC1-FP-BIT-EVIDENCE.md`: the correspondence table, RAC1 results, the pinned rac1-decomp commit and the `fp-bit.c` SHA-256, and what a RAC2 trial must still show. The GPL sources are referenced, not copied;
- plans one queued research task, `boot-fp-bit-verbatim-source-rac1-e

merged.title: docs: summarise rac1-decomp findings that bear on RAC2
merged.author: Lynder063
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Adds `docs/RAC1-DECOMP-FINDINGS.md` and a README link to it. The page summarises results measured by [rac1-decomp](https://github.com/OpenRAC/rac1-decomp) (`SCES_509.16`, 22.6% of code matched) that concern compiler, library and SDK code shared by the engine's games:

1. **libgcc from GCC's own sources** with Sony's 2.9-ee-991111, the lineage of this repo's GNU EE profile. Covers the source revisions, the fp-bit configuration macros, building through the driver rather than `cc1`, one object per `L_*` module, and the modules still open.
2. **EE SDK archives as a source of names.** Includes the caveat that RAC2's toolchain policy requires verified provenance.
3. **Compiler behaviour measured on RAC1**, for understanding only, because RAC1's assembly rewriting is not acceptable here. Covers the SN v1.14 vs v1.36 callee-saved slot layout, missing sibling calls, `-G2` and the short-loop erratum.
4. **m2c and decomp-permuter** as candidate generators that feed the normal campaign

merged.title: decomp: match the boot's fp-bit single-precision unpacker from vendored libgcc
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## Result

Integrates the 144-byte boot single-precision unpacker `FUN_00123400` from
pinned libgcc source. Proposed exact C coverage is 311,644 / 48,788,176 bytes
(0.6388%), up by 144 bytes. No native overlay body is newly credited.

## Source and licensing

The vendored source is derived from GCC 2.95.3 fp-bit.c at the upstream commit
and SHA-256 recorded in `src/libgcc/README.md`. Its preprocessed program text
has one mechanical unpacker-symbol rename; the refused `fptodp` keeps its
original name. The program text between the markers is unchanged by the
corrective commit.

The original FSF copyright, GPL version 2-or-later notice, disclaimer, author
credits, additional linking permissions and special exception are retained.
`src/libgcc/COPYING` supplies the complete GPLv2 text. One trailing space in an
upstream comment is normalized separately from the unchanged program body.
The README identifies the same GPL portion in generated `candidates/boot.c`;
the surround

merged.title: tooling: discover shared families and prepare exact binding trials
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
Common C functions recur at different addresses in Going Commando's level overlays. This adds a maintained workflow to discover candidate copies and prepare one reviewed C body with explicit per-program bindings, while keeping complete unmasked byte equality as the acceptance rule.

The discovery tool validates pinned EE references and complete non-overlapping intervals, then masks only J/JAL destination bits. Constants, GP/address halves, COP2 operands and trailing NOPs remain visible. Reports are private metadata and add no matching credit or unique-code denominator.

The preparer verifies canonical fragments/context, current recipes, native catalogues and complete-unit reviews before creating a fresh private bank. Its portable tasks split the existing G0/G8 profiles and use the unchanged campaign compiler/linker/checker. The reviewed GS spec, workflow documentation and preserved positive/negative pilot make this reproducible.

Validation:
- Public CLI: one GS candidate group with 27
